Marcus / Monica —

Quick finance readout from my side after a first pass: 

- Scenario A (price hold + 10% uplift on base commit): gives Nimbus predictability and keeps unit price stable. Estimated impact: ~+3.2% on ARR vs renewal at current rates. Minimal billing complexity.
- Scenario B (20% discount for +25% commit): lowers unit economics but increases committed revenue; estimated impact: +12.4% ARR with lower gross margin. Good for us if Nimbus reliably hits the higher commit.
- One-time service credit: recommend offering a $15,000 credit tied to a remediation confirmation (they must acknowledge incident and accept credit in amendment). This keeps bookkeeping simple and is small relative to expected renewal.

Recommended: present both options to Nimbus but push for Scenario B as our preferred path with an explicit milestone (quarterly reporting) to validate commit attainment. Monica, confirm if burst credits can be implemented as prepaid buckets that auto-consume during peak windows; if so we'll propose a base + 100k token burst bucket at a modest premium.

-Neha
Director, Revenue Finance
Redwood Inference

Thanks for the quick turnaround and for modeling both approaches. Nimbus is comfortable moving forward with Scenario B (deeper discount + 25% higher commit) provided we include: 

- A prepaid burst bucket (100k token equivalent) that rolls forward one month only.
- The $15,000 service credit applied to the first invoice after effective date.
- Quarterly usage checkpoints with Redwood CSM and the ability to true-up over the quarter if usage misses commit by >15%.

Please send an updated SOW and amendment with those terms and we can loop Procurement for signatures. If you can get the draft by EOD Monday that would keep us on track for an Oct 1 start.
